arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Syngenta cites Kikkonen v. Guardian Life to support removal of retained jurisdiction cases.
Henson asserts Congress defines removal limits, including original jurisdiction requirements.
Chief Justice Rehnquist noted the case is submitted after hearing both advocates.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This dispute centers on federal removal power. Syngenta wants to move a state class action to federal court. Henson argues federal courts cannot accept cases lacking original jurisdiction.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 15, 2002.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Syngenta wants the Supreme Court to allow removal of the state class action to federal court.
Henson wants the Supreme Court to deny removal and keep the case in state court.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 22, lines 15-35
Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 17-3

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Syngenta argues the All Writs Act permits removal when a state court retains jurisdiction over a settlement.
Henson argues the All Writs Act cannot remove cases that federal courts lack original jurisdiction to hear.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Does the All Writs Act allow removal of a state class action settlement to federal court?
Can a federal court accept a case where the state court retained jurisdiction to manage the settlement?

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 34, lines 41-41

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between state and federal court authority. It determines whether companies can move class action settlements to federal courts. The outcome shapes access to federal forums for complex civil disputes.
